findings.element: 2026 Forecast Scenarios — Institution Comparison table (Key View and As Of columns)
findings.detail: The 'Key View' and 'As Of' columns in the institution comparison table contain very small, dense text that is extremely difficult to read at dashboard viewing scale. Multiple rows of narrative text are compressed into narrow cells, making them illegible for a CEO-level audience.

findings.element: Sector tiles (Passenger Airlines, Hotels, Restaurants, etc.) — commentary text
findings.detail: The body commentary text within each sector tile (e.g., 'Stamp', 'Clamp', 'Macro' labels and associated narrative) is rendered at an extremely small font size, making it unreadable without zooming in. This is below the minimum legible size for a board-level presentation.

findings.element: Key 2025 Actuals & 2026 Themes — numbered bullet commentary
findings.detail: The six numbered bullet points at the bottom of the page are rendered in very small font. The dense paragraph text is difficult to read at normal dashboard resolution, particularly for a board deck context.

findings.element: 2025 Quarterly GDP — BEA Estimates bar chart (x-axis labels)
findings.detail: The x-axis quarter labels (Q1 2025, Q2 2025, etc.) and the 'Q1 2026' label appear compressed and partially cut off at the right edge of the chart area.

findings.element: fc-note commentary block (Real GDP growth paragraph)
findings.detail: The commentary note ('Real GDP growth of 2.0% annualized is holding above stall speed…') appears to be placed above the charts on this tab, which is correct in position, but it is rendered as a very small-font block that is difficult to distinguish as the leading editorial note. However, verifying exact placement relative to the first chart is borderline — the block does precede the charts visually.

findings.element: fc-note commentary block (Real GDP growth paragraph)
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging language ('could provide temporary offsets') and runs as a single long run-on sentence that exceeds the 4-sentence maximum. The style guide requires 2–4 sentences with no hedging filler.

findings.element: 2024 vs 2025 vs 2026F — Key Macro Indicators chart (axis labels and bar labels)
findings.detail: The grouped bar chart on the right side of the GDP section has very small axis tick labels and data labels on the bars that are nearly illegible at the rendered size. Category labels on the x-axis are compressed and hard to distinguish.

findings.element: Sector tiles grid (bottom section)
findings.detail: The sector tiles (12 tiles across two rows) show inconsistent vertical heights — the second row tiles (Pharmaceuticals, Residential Real Estate, Commercial RE, Auto Manufacturing, Federal Government, Freight & Logistics) appear taller than the first row tiles, creating uneven spacing and misalignment across the grid.

findings.element: Sector tiles — first row vs second row
findings.detail: Vertical spacing and tile height visibly differ between the first row of sector tiles and the second row, breaking the uniform grid layout expected for peer panels.

findings.element: Source citations beneath charts and tables
findings.detail: Source attribution lines (e.g., 'SOURCES: GOLDMAN SACHS MACRO OUTLOOK JAN 2026…') are rendered at an extremely small font size throughout the page, making them effectively invisible without zooming. While source lines are typically small, they should remain minimally legible.

findings.element: Sector panel commentary text (all sector cards)
findings.detail: The commentary text beneath each sector bar chart is rendered at an extremely small font size (appears to be ~6-7px), making it completely unreadable at normal viewing scale. This would be embarrassing in a board deck.

findings.element: Annual chart data vintage / methodology footnote below sector filter bar
findings.detail: The footnote line ('ANNUAL-CHART DATA VINTAGE · PINNED TO ALIGN AS OF 2026-04-01 · REFRESH CADENCE: QUARTERLY…') is rendered in very small, low-contrast gray text that is effectively illegible without zooming in.

findings.element: Broad Sector Groups table — 2026F 'Trend' column values
findings.detail: The 'Trend' column in the Broad Sector Groups table shows colored pill labels (e.g., 'Falling', 'Slowing') but the text inside the pills is extremely small and difficult to read at dashboard scale.

findings.element: KPI metric tile sub-labels and prior-period annotations (top header row)
findings.detail: The secondary annotation lines beneath each KPI tile (e.g., 'Prior: +130K (Mar'26)', 'FOMC range: 5.00–5.75', etc.) are rendered at a very small size and low contrast, making them difficult to read without zooming.

findings.element: GDP Commentary block — body paragraph
findings.detail: The commentary paragraph text appears to be cut off at the right edge of the commentary box on some lines, suggesting the container width may be clipping the text rather than wrapping cleanly.

findings.element: GDP Commentary — 'GDP Commentary — 2025 Growth & 2026 Outlook' block
findings.detail: The commentary block appears above the KPI summary tiles but below the tab navigation bar. However, the sector-level mini-commentary notes appear below each sector chart rather than preceding them, violating the rule that fc-note commentary must precede the first chart it annotates.

findings.element: Broad Sector Groups table — source footnote at bottom
findings.detail: The sources footnote at the very bottom of the page is rendered in extremely small gray text, effectively invisible at normal resolution.

findings.element: Sector bar chart panels — year-over-year percentage labels on bars
findings.detail: In several sector panels (e.g., Software/Cloud, Inv. Banking, Chips/Hardware), the percentage change labels on the small bar charts appear to overlap adjacent bar labels due to the compressed panel width, making individual values indistinguishable.

findings.element: Jobs tab
findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: Unemployment tab
findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: Monthly Wage Growth chart — source/footnote text below chart
findings.detail: The source line and footnote text beneath the Monthly Wage Growth (13-Month Trend) chart is rendered at an extremely small font size, making it effectively unreadable at normal viewing scale. This would be called out in a board-level review.

findings.element: Nominal vs Real Wage Growth — Annual History chart — source/footnote text
findings.detail: Source and footnote text beneath the Annual History chart is rendered at a font size too small to read without significant zoom, inconsistent with board-deck legibility standards.

findings.element: Wage Growth by Sector table — source footnote at bottom
findings.detail: The multi-line source/methodology footnote at the bottom of the sector table is rendered at a very small size and low contrast, making it illegible at dashboard viewing distance.

findings.element: Page-level footer (very bottom of screenshot)
findings.detail: The footer row containing data vintage, pipeline, and attribution text is rendered at an extremely small font size and is effectively unreadable.

findings.element: Wage Growth by Sector table — 'Trend' column badges
findings.detail: Every single row in the Trend column shows a red 'Falling' badge. If 'Falling' is a warning or critical semantic state, the color should match the style_guide §4 palette for those roles. A uniform red across all 19 rows with no variation suggests either a data/rendering error or a color assignment that has not been validated against the palette.

findings.element: Avg Hourly Earnings by Sector — 2025 vs 2024 chart — Y-axis sector labels
findings.detail: Several sector label strings on the Y-axis of the horizontal bar chart appear to be truncated or very tightly clipped against the bar area, with longer names (e.g., 'Hotel Front Desk / Hou...', 'Airline Pilots & Crew') potentially cut off, reducing readability for a CEO audience.

findings.element: Wage Growth Commentary block
findings.detail: The 'Wage Growth Commentary — Nominal vs Real' fc-note block appears above the metric tiles and charts on this tab, which is correct in principle; however, it is separated from the first chart by a large block of KPI tiles and data-vintage metadata. Style_guide §1 requires the fc-note to immediately precede the first chart with no intervening content panels between them.

findings.element: Wage Growth Commentary — Nominal vs Real
findings.detail: The commentary block contains a single very long run-on sentence that functions as one sentence rather than the required 2–4 sentences. Style_guide §2 mandates 2–4 sentences; a single compound sentence stitched with semicolons does not satisfy that requirement and reads as hedging filler at board level.

findings.element: Gap between Monthly Wage Growth chart and Nominal vs Real / Sector bar charts row
findings.detail: The vertical spacing between the Monthly Wage Growth (13-Month Trend) panel and the two-column panel row below it appears noticeably larger than the spacing between subsequent panels, creating an inconsistent rhythm across the tab.

findings.element: Trimmed-mean and median CPI track headline — bottom chart
findings.detail: The chart area displays 'AWAITING FIRST PIPELINE RUN' placeholder text with a note that data will populate next week. The chart is effectively blank with no plotted data, making it unsuitable for a board-level deck.

findings.element: Trimmed-mean and median CPI track headline — bottom chart
findings.detail: The line chart shows lines that appear to stop and not render across the full time series, consistent with the pipeline not having run. The series are present in the legend but absent from the plot area.

findings.element: Trimmed-mean and median CPI — 'So what' commentary
findings.detail: The 'So what' sentence reads as a single sentence of analytical commentary, which may fall below the minimum of 2 sentences required by the style guide. Additionally the placeholder pipeline note embedded in the chart body is not editorial copy and should not be visible to a CEO audience.

findings.element: Annual CPI bar chart — x-axis year labels
findings.detail: The year labels along the x-axis of the 'Annual CPI is still well above the Fed's 2% target' chart are extremely small and difficult to read at normal viewing distance, falling below acceptable contrast and size standards for a board presentation.

findings.element: Category-level annual rates table — body text
findings.detail: The text within the category-level annual rates table (category names, percentage values, and trend labels) is rendered at a very small font size, making it difficult to read without zooming in, which is inappropriate for CEO-level board material.

findings.element: KPI metric tiles — top row sub-labels
findings.detail: Several metric tiles in the top KPI row have sub-label text (prior period comparisons and footnotes) that appears clipped or compressed within the tile boundaries, particularly on the rightmost tiles (e.g., Debt Service Ratio tile).

findings.element: CPI Commentary — Inflation Trajectory & Fed Implications
findings.detail: The fc-note commentary block appears above the KPI summary tiles and charts as expected, but it sits below the tab navigation bar and filter row rather than immediately preceding the first chart panel. Depending on style_guide interpretation this may violate the requirement that commentary precedes the first chart.

findings.element: Source footnotes — all chart panels
findings.detail: Source citation text beneath each chart panel is rendered at an extremely small font size with low contrast against the white background, making it effectively illegible without magnification.

findings.element: Bottom source/footnote text block
findings.detail: The dense source citations and footnote text at the very bottom of the dashboard are rendered at an extremely small font size (appears to be ~6–7px), making them effectively unreadable at normal viewing scale. This would be called out in a board presentation.

findings.element: Delinquency Rates by Product chart — axis labels and data labels
findings.detail: The x-axis year labels and several inline data point labels on the 90+ DPD line chart are very small and densely packed, making individual values difficult to read without zooming in.

findings.element: Senior Loan Officer Survey (SLOOS) chart — Risk Intensity Timeline rows
findings.detail: The row labels and cell text within the Risk Intensity Timeline heatmap band beneath the SLOOS chart are rendered at a very small size and low contrast against the colored cells, making them illegible at dashboard scale.

findings.element: Consumer Credit Growth chart — x-axis labels
findings.detail: Year labels on the x-axis of the Revolving vs Non-Revolving YoY % bar chart are very small and may be difficult to read in a projected board setting.

findings.element: Delinquency Rates by Product — inline data labels
findings.detail: Multiple inline percentage labels on the line chart overlap each other, particularly in the 2020–2024 region where Credit Cards, Auto Loans, and Mortgage lines converge, making individual values indistinguishable.

findings.element: Net Charge-Off Rates chart — bar labels
findings.detail: Several data labels on the grouped bar chart for Card Specialists vs Diversified Banks appear to overlap or sit very close together, reducing readability.

findings.element: Credit Commentary — Spread Complacency & Tail Risk
findings.detail: The commentary block contains a single very long run-on sentence that exceeds the 4-sentence maximum and uses hedging language ('suggests high yield is also mispriced relative to…'). Style guide requires 2–4 sentences with no hedging filler.

findings.element: Household Debt Composition & Stress table — SIGNAL column badges
findings.detail: The colored signal badges (e.g., 'STRESS', 'CAUTION', 'MONITOR') in the table appear to have inconsistent sizing and padding across rows, with some badge text appearing clipped or unevenly padded relative to peers.

findings.element: Metric tiles row (top KPI bar)
findings.detail: The spacing between the 'JOBS APR'26' tile and the 'INITIAL CLAIMS MAY'26' tile appears slightly wider than the spacing between subsequent tiles, creating a subtle but visible inconsistency in the top KPI row.

findings.element: Household Debt Composition table — Total HH Debt SIGNAL badge
findings.detail: The 'LATE-CYCLE' signal badge on the Total HH Debt row uses a dark/navy color that does not clearly map to the dashboard's established critical/warning/confirmed semantic palette, creating ambiguity about its severity level for a CEO-level reader.

findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: Monthly Housing Trend — Case-Shiller YoY % & 30yr Mortgage Rate (13-Month) — source note
findings.detail: The source/footnote text beneath the dual-panel line chart is rendered at an extremely small font size (appears to be ~6–7 px), making it effectively unreadable at normal viewing distance in a board deck.

findings.element: Affordability Index & Months Supply — x-axis labels (lower panel)
findings.detail: Year labels on the x-axis of the Months Supply sub-panel are extremely small and densely packed, making individual year values illegible without zooming in.

findings.element: Affordability Index & Months Supply — x-axis labels
findings.detail: The x-axis tick labels on both the Affordability Index and Months Supply sub-panels appear to overlap or nearly collide due to the high density of annual labels across a long time series, reducing readability.

findings.element: 30-Year Mortgage Rate vs Fed Funds Rate — data point labels
findings.detail: The value callout labels on the line chart (e.g., rate percentages annotated at each data point) are very small and low-contrast against the chart background, making them difficult to read in a board presentation context.

findings.element: Home Price Index — Case-Shiller & FHFA — source note
findings.detail: Source attribution text below the chart is rendered at a very small size (~6 px), falling below the minimum legible threshold for a CEO-level board deck.

findings.element: Housing Starts — Single-Family vs Multi-Family — source note
findings.detail: Source attribution text below the chart is rendered at a very small size, consistent with the pattern across all chart footnotes on this tab.

findings.element: Housing Commentary — Affordability Crisis & Lock-In Effect
findings.detail: The commentary block contains five distinct sentences, exceeding the maximum of 4 sentences permitted by the style guide. The passage also contains hedging language ('would be a significant recessionary signal') that softens the analytical stance beyond what is appropriate for a CEO audience.

findings.element: Metro Home Price Performance table — 'Detroit, MI' row
findings.detail: The Detroit row is bolded ('Fastest-appreciating major market from low base; UAW effect') while all other Market Note cells are in regular weight, creating an inconsistent visual treatment within the table that appears unintentional rather than a deliberate hierarchy signal.

findings.element: Monthly Housing Trend — 30yr Mortgage Rate sub-panel
findings.detail: The lower sub-panel of the dual-panel Monthly Housing Trend chart shows only a legend label ('30yr Mortgage Rate %') in the chart header area but no color swatch legend is visible within or adjacent to the panel itself, which could cause confusion if the chart is viewed in isolation.

findings.element: Oil Supply Shock Tracker — Daily Closes (Section 2 left chart)
findings.detail: The x-axis date labels and source footnote text in the daily closes chart are extremely small and unreadable at dashboard viewing scale. Tick labels appear to be 6–7px, well below the minimum legible body size.

findings.element: WTI & Brent — Monthly Jan 2022–Feb 2026 (Section 1 right chart) axis labels

findings.element: WTI Price History with Recession Shading 1973–2025 (Section 4 left chart) axis and source labels

findings.element: WTI & Brent — Monthly Jan 2022–Feb 2026 (Section 1 right chart)
findings.detail: The 'Hormuz shock, May 2025' annotation label appears to overlap with the price spike data point and the chart's right-side legend/color key, creating a cluttered, hard-to-parse area in the upper right of the chart.

findings.element: Section 4 — Recession Signal History commentary block
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging language ('Worth monitoring if prices re-escalate or persist above $90 for an extended period') which is speculative filler rather than a direct analytical assertion. Style guide prohibits hedging filler in fc-note commentary.

findings.element: Section 2 — Inflation Transmission commentary / section label
findings.detail: The 'SECTION 2 — INFLATION TRANSMISSION' label and its associated note text appear to sit between charts rather than clearly preceding the first chart in that section, which may violate the requirement that fc-note commentary precede the first chart.

findings.element: Full Oil Impact Chain — Prices to Credit Stress (Section 2 right panel) body text
findings.detail: The descriptive sub-text beneath each numbered node (e.g., Route 1.0, Route 2.0, etc.) is rendered at approximately 7–8px and is illegible at board presentation scale without zooming.

findings.element: Historical Oil Shock Episodes table — Economic Consequence column
findings.detail: The 'Economic Consequence' column text in the bottom-right table is very small and low-contrast against the white background, making it difficult to read in a board deck context.

findings.element: Section 1 vs Section 2 panel spacing
findings.detail: The vertical gap between Section 1 (Price & Supply) and Section 2 (Inflation Transmission) appears noticeably tighter than the gap between Section 2 and Section 3 (Sector Impact), creating inconsistent inter-panel rhythm across the tab.
